name: Upstream Open Reading Frame (uORF) Blocking
therapeuticGoalDescription: Increase translation of the primary open reading frame (pORF) by preventing translation initiation at inhibitory upstream open reading frames (uORFs).
molecularDefect: Reduced protein expression due to translational repression mediated by functional uORFs within the 5′ UTR.
diseaseMechanism: Translation initiation at a uORF decreases translation of the downstream coding sequence. Steric-blocking ASOs mask the uORF start site or regulatory sequence to favor translation of the primary ORF.
suitableVariantTypes: Disorders where reduced protein expression is directly attributable to a validated inhibitory uORF.
typicalDiseases: No established disease indication. Published work has focused primarily on proof-of-concept and experimental targets.
rnaTargetRegion: 5′ untranslated region (5′ UTR), specifically inhibitory uORFs and their AUG initiation codons.
transcriptRequirement: Target transcript must contain a functionally validated inhibitory uORF regulating translation of the primary ORF.
asoChemistry: RNase H-inactive steric-blocking ASOs (e.g., fully modified phosphorothioate/2′-MOE designs in the original studies).
typicalLength: Approximately 16–20 nt in the original studies; no universal standard established.
designRules: Literature synthesis: identify functional uORFs experimentally; target the uAUG or adjacent regulatory sequence; avoid RNase H-mediated cleavage; validate translational effects experimentally.
secondaryStructureRequirement: Accessible 5′ UTR regions surrounding the uORF initiation site are preferred.
offTargetConsiderations: Potential effects on translation of non-target transcripts containing homologous 5′ UTR sequences; transcriptome-wide specificity analysis recommended.
advantages: Potential to increase endogenous protein production without altering genomic DNA or degrading the target transcript.
limitations: Independent studies have questioned the reproducibility of this strategy for some targets (e.g., RNASEH1). Clinical utility remains unproven.

evidenceLevel.note: Strong mechanistic rationale but conflicting experimental evidence and no clinical validation.

referencesSummary: Liang et al. (2016); Liang et al. (2017); Ahlskog et al. (2025).
